host_timing_note: Measured on the FreeRTOS POSIX port, where every task is a thread of a Linux process. Times, jitter and latencies are those of the host's scheduler and are not what the same code shows on a microcontroller; counts, orderings and sizes of protocol data are independent of the host. The outcomes of the trials are decided by the node and the flash, not the host's clock; only the times per trial and the wall time are the host's, with the workers running in parallel.

config.cuts: armed on the command line (--flash-cut N:SEED of fcn_flash, fcn_boot or the node); none at run time
config.transport: udp, a bus of the trial's own ports; the node's default 500 kbit/s
config.flash_waits: fcn_flash --no-wait; fcn_boot and the node wait the modelled times

legend.trials: one line per trial, its columns (as named) separated by |, the starts by ;, an absent value empty (fcn_tools.powerloss.parse_row() reads it): class, sequence and op (the operation cut, numbered in its sequence; fcn_tools.powerloss), seed (the cut's), role (what the operation writes), program (whose --flash-cut N counts it), cut (the FATAL line: the position cut of the positions and the transitions done of all), tear (none, some or all of the transitions done; nothing: the torn unit or sector had no bit to change), before (the state before the operation, from the model), after (the state the cut left, read both ways), left (before or after: which of the two it is), boot (what the first start after the cut did), starts (every start until a confirmed image ran, with its exit status), follow_up (the next update), lock_retries, seconds (the trial's wall time), check (the check that failed; its message is in failures)
legend.sequences: per sequence its operations: the number, the kind, address+length, the role, the start of the board that makes it, the program and its N (of --flash-cut N), the state before -> the state after (the model's)
legend.state: slot A and slot B as letters (E empty, W writing, T trial, C confirmed, P previous, R rejected), the newest record's sequence number:event, aN the trial's attempts used, uN the log's entries in use
legend.start: the slot, then t<attempt> for a trial or c for the confirmed image, and the bootloader's event if it wrote one (ROLLBACK)
legend.replay: python bench/power_loss.py --replay <class>:<sequence>:<op>:<seed> runs a trial again, the same way, and keeps its files
